pages.title: Unit 1: First Day at School (Poem)
bulletPoints: I wonder if my drawing will be as good as theirs;
I wonder if they’ll like me or just be full of stares;
I wonder if my teacher will look like Mom or Gran;
I wonder if my puppy will wonder where I am.

pages.title: Unit 1: Haldi’s Adventure
bulletPoints: One morning, as Haldi walked to school, she met a giraffe named Smiley.
Smiley wore large round spectacles and held a book in his furry hand.
Haldi was surprised: "I have never met a giraffe wearing glasses and holding a book!"
Smiley invited Haldi to climb onto his back; she rode high above, learning about stars, trees, and birds.

pages.title: Unit 2: I am Lucky! (Poem)
bulletPoints: If I were a butterfly, I would be thankful for my wings.
If I were a myna in a tree, I would be thankful that I could sing.
If I were a fish in the sea, I would be thankful that I can wriggle and giggle with glee.
So I just think I am lucky to be me, not you, but me!

pages.title: Unit 2: I Want (The Clever Monkey)
bulletPoints: Little Monkey said: "I want to be big, I want to be strong!" A wise woman heard him with a magic wand.
He asked for a giraffe's long neck, an elephant's water-spraying trunk, and a zebra's black-and-white stripes.
Looking into the river, he saw a scary monster with stripes, a trunk, and a long neck—and screamed in terror!
He cried: "Mother, I want to be myself again!" With a pop, bang, and whiz, he became a happy little monkey once more.

pages.title: Unit 3: A Smile (Poem)
bulletPoints: A smile is quite a funny thing, It wrinkles up your face;
And when it’s gone you’ll never find Its secret hiding place.
But far more wonderful it is To see what smiles can do:
You smile at one, he smiles at you, And so one smile makes two!

pages.title: Unit 3: The Wind and the Sun
bulletPoints: The Wind boasted: "Sun, see that man walking down the road? I can get his coat off faster than you!"
Wind blew hard: WHOOOOO! The trees bent, but the man pulled his coat tight and buttoned it up.
The Sun said: "Now let me try." The Sun shone warmly, and the man unbuttoned his coat.
The Sun shone hotter and hotter until the man wiped his brow and took off his coat in relief!

pages.title: Unit 4: Rain (Poem)
bulletPoints: The rain is raining all around, It falls on field and tree;
It rains on the umbrellas here, And on the ships at sea.
Puddles on the ground: Splashing in red gumboots and floating paper boats down little gutters.
Where does rain go? Rain feeds the roots of flowers, fills sparkling mountain brooks, and nourishes the soil.

pages.title: Unit 4: Storm in the Garden (Sunu-sunu the Snail)
bulletPoints: Sunu-sunu, the little snail, was visiting his friends, the garden ants.
Suddenly: CRASH! White lightning flashed through the garden clouds: ZZZZT! ZZZZT!
Thunder rolled: GADAM! GUDUM! The ants hid under flowerpots and called: "Hurry home, Sunu-sunu!"
Sunu-sunu tucked his head into his shell, tucked his tail into his shell, and sat still—safe from the storm!

pages.title: Unit 5: Zoo Manners (Poem)
bulletPoints: Be careful what you say or do When you visit the animals at the Zoo.
Don’t make fun of the Camel’s hump—He’s very proud of his noble bump.
Don’t laugh too much at the Chimpanzee—He thinks he’s as wise as you or me!
Treat them as well as they do you, And you’ll always be welcome at the Zoo.

pages.title: Unit 5: Funny Bunny: The Sky is Falling!
bulletPoints: One day, a nut fell right on Funny Bunny's head: Ouch! "The sky is falling!" he cried.
He ran to tell the King, meeting Henny Penny, Cocky Locky, Ducky Lucky, and Poosey Goosey.
They all panicked: "The sky is falling, we are going to tell the King!"
Cunning Woxy Foxy said: "The King lives this way, follow me!" and led the foolish birds away!

pages.title: Unit 6: Mr. Nobody (Poem)
bulletPoints: I know a funny little man, As quiet as a mouse,
Who does the mischief that is done In everybody’s house!
There’s no one ever sees his face, And yet we all agree
That every plate we break was cracked By Mr. Nobody!

pages.title: Unit 6: Curlylocks and the Three Bears
bulletPoints: Curlylocks had curly golden hair. She walked into the woods and saw the cottage of the Bear family.
Three bowls of porridge on the table: Papa Bear's big bowl was too hot; Mama Bear's middle bowl was too cold.
Baby Bear's tiny bowl was just right! Curlylocks ate it all up, sat on Baby Bear's tiny chair until it broke!
She slept in Baby Bear's tiny bed; when the Bears returned, Curlylocks woke with a jump and ran away!

pages.title: Unit 7: On My Blackboard I Can Draw (Poem)
bulletPoints: On my blackboard I can draw: One little house with one green door,
Two brown gates that open wide, Three red steps that lead inside,
Four little chimneys painted white, Five little windows shining bright,
Six yellow marigolds straight and tall, Growing up against the wall!

pages.title: Unit 7: Make It Shorter (Akbar and Birbal)
bulletPoints: Emperor Akbar drew a chalk line on the palace floor and ordered his courtiers: "Make this line shorter without erasing any part of it."
All the wise ministers looked at the line in silence; no one knew what to do.
Birbal smiled, stepped forward, and drew a longer chalk line right next to Akbar's line.
Everyone saw: Akbar's line was now clearly shorter than Birbal's line! Akbar applauded Birbal’s wit.

pages.title: Unit 8: I am the Music Man (Poem)
bulletPoints: I am the music man, I come from far away, And I can play! What can you play?
I play the piano: Pia-pia-piano, piano, piano; Pia-pia-piano, pia-piano!
I play the big bass drum: Boomdi-boomdi-boomdi-boom, boomdi-boom, boomdi-boom!
Rhythm and melody: Music fills our hearts with joy, dancing, and harmony.

pages.title: Unit 8: The Mumbai Musicians
bulletPoints: Gopu the donkey had worked hard for many years carrying heavy sacks of corn.
He was tired and old, so his master said: "Go see the world and become a musician!"
On the road to Mumbai, Gopu was joined by Dopu the dog, Kopu the cat, and Furry the cock.
They reached a house with dinner, sang together to earn food: The people thought ghosts had arrived and fled!

pages.title: Unit 9: Granny Granny Please Comb My Hair (Poem)
bulletPoints: Granny, Granny, Please comb my hair; You always take your time, You always take such care.
You put me on a cushion Between your knees; You rub a little coconut oil, Gentle as a breeze.
You part my hair so neat and clean, And when you are done, You smile and say: "Now, who is my nice little girl?"

pages.title: Unit 9: The Magic Porridge Pot
bulletPoints: A poor kind girl named Tara met an old woman in the forest who gifted her a magic clay pot.
Say: "Cook-Pot-Cook" and it cooks sweet porridge; say: "Stop-Pot-Stop" and it stops cooking.
One day Tara was out; her mother said "Cook-Pot-Cook" and ate happily, but forgot the stopping words!
Porridge overflowed the pot, flooded the floor, poured into the street! Tara ran home shouting: "Stop-Pot-Stop!"

pages.title: Unit 10: Strange Talk & English Master Celebration
bulletPoints: A little green frog lived under a log, And every time he spoke, Instead of saying "Good morning," he only said, "Croak-croak."
A duck lived by the waterside, And little did he lack, But when we asked, "How do you do?" he only said, "Quack-quack."
A little pig lived in a sty, As fat as he could be, And when he asked for dinner, he only said, "Wee-wee."
Class 2 English Champion: You have mastered stories, fables, and songs with confidence and expressive joy!
